title: Lessons from the Demise of a Voting Rights Bill

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责报道《纽约时报》每日简讯

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: Dealbook的商业与政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 在11月18日，我将在纽约市Dealbook峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的领袖，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、佐兰·莫达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在nytimes.com上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Valparo.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·瓦尔帕罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是每日简报。

sentences.en: Today, the most sweeping expansion of federal voting rights in a generation, died last night in the
sentences.zh: 今天，整整一代人中规模最大的一次联邦投票权扩展法案，昨晚在

sentences.en: U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: Senate.
sentences.zh: 参议院夭折了。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, congressional reporter Nick Thandos, about what we learned from its demise.
sentences.zh: 我与我的同事、国会记者尼克·桑多斯谈论了我们从中吸取的教训。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, June 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月23日，星期三。

sentences.en: Um, where, where are you?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你在，你在哪里？

sentences.en: It looks like you're in a radio studio.
sentences.zh: 看起来你在一个广播室里。

sentences.en: Yeah, isn't this nifty?
sentences.zh: 对啊，这不是很棒吗？

sentences.en: I'm in a audio booth in the House Daily Press Gallery, right outside the
sentences.zh: 我在众议院日常记者招待会的音频间里，就在

sentences.en: House chamber.
sentences.zh: 众议院议事厅外面。

sentences.en: I come here because it's nice and quiet.
sentences.zh: 我来这里是因为这里又好又安静。

sentences.en: So basically, the House of Representatives has, like, podcast studios.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，众议院里有类似播客工作室的东西。

sentences.en: Uh, something like that.
sentences.zh: 呃，差不多吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, you've never sounded better.
sentences.zh: 是啊，你的声音听起来从来没这么好过。

sentences.en: In fact, you've always sounded worse.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你以前的声音总是很糟糕。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, it's better.
sentences.zh: 对，不，现在更好听了。

sentences.en: I'm, like, jealous because it actually sounds better than I do.
sentences.zh: 我甚至有点嫉妒，因为这听起来确实比我好。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's just jump in, Nick.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我们直接切入正题吧，尼克。

sentences.en: Can you describe what just happened in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下刚刚在美国

sentences.en: Capitol?
sentences.zh: 国会大厦发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: So after months of debating and promising and fighting over it, the United States Senate finally held a vote on Democrats' big, gargantuan election overhaul bill called the
sentences.zh: 所以在经历了几个月的辩论、承诺和争吵之后，美国参议院终于对民主党人庞大的、巨型的选举改革法案进行了投票，该法案被称为

sentences.en: For the People Act.
sentences.zh: 《为人民法案》。

sentences.en: And so I rise, Mr. President, with what I think is a simple request of my colleagues.
sentences.zh: 议长先生，我起立提出我认为是我的同僚们的一个简单请求。

sentences.en: Let's do our job.
sentences.zh: 让我们做好我们的工作。

sentences.en: And let's have a principled conversation about voting rights.
sentences.zh: 让我们就投票权展开一场有原则的对话。

sentences.en: Let's have that conversation right here, right now.
sentences.zh: 让我们就在这里、就在此时此刻展开这场对话。

sentences.en: How could we do otherwise?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么能不做呢？

sentences.en: This wasn't even a vote on the merits of the bill.
sentences.zh: 这甚至不是对法案实质内容的投票。

sentences.en: It was a vote just to start debate, to consider it and potentially consider alternatives to it.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是一次关于是否开始辩论、是否审议该法案以及潜在考虑其替代方案的投票。

sentences.en: The Senate will vote on whether to advance Democrats' transparently partisan plan to tilt permanently in their favor.
sentences.zh: 参议院将就是否推进民主党人公开偏袒自身利益的计划进行投票。

sentences.en: And what we saw happen, which was not entirely surprising, is that Republicans stood firm on a vow that they've made for months now to block this bill.
sentences.zh: 而我们看到的情况是——这并不完全令人意外——共和党人坚守了他们几个月前许下的誓言，要阻止这项法案。

sentences.en: By now, the rotten inner workings of this power grab have been thoroughly exposed to the light.
sentences.zh: 到现在为止，这场争夺权力背后的腐败运作已经完全暴露在阳光下了。

sentences.en: And they all voted to prevent debate from moving forward.
sentences.zh: 他们都投票阻止辩论继续推进。

sentences.en: Today, the Senate's going to fulfill our founding purpose, stop the partisan power grab and reject
sentences.zh: 今天，参议院将履行我们建国的宗旨，阻止党派权力争夺并拒绝

sentences.en: as one filibustering the bill and effectively leaving it for dead, at least for now on the Senate floor.
sentences.zh: 正如一方对法案进行冗长辩论并实际上将其束之高阁一样，至少目前在参议院大厅是这样的。

sentences.en: So this is the filibuster very much in action.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是正在发挥作用的冗长辩论。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We've been hearing about it since Democrats took control in January, right, that the filibuster
sentences.zh: 自从民主党人在1月接管国会以来，我们一直听到关于它的消息，对吧？冗长辩论

sentences.en: was going to be the main obstacle to their agenda on a whole host of issues from guns to immigration to voting rights.
sentences.zh: 将成为他们议程的主要障碍，涉及从枪支到移民再到投票权的许多议题。

sentences.en: And this was it in action today.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天实际发生的情况。

sentences.en: And for those who don't quite know or have been pretending to know exactly what it means
sentences.zh: 对于那些不太了解或者自从民主党控制参议院以来一直假装确切知道冗长辩论意味着什么的人来说

sentences.en: to filibuster since Democrats took control of the Senate, can you just describe what it actually
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下，共和党人今天所做的事情——也就是利用冗长辩论来扼杀一项立法——到底

sentences.en: means to have done what Republicans did today, which is to use the filibuster to kill a piece of legislation?
sentences.zh: 意味着什么吗？

sentences.en: Michael, I'm glad you asked that because it is often misunderstood even by those who pretend to know Congress.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，很高兴你问了这个，因为即使是对国会装懂的人也经常误解这一点。

sentences.en: So the Senate's filibuster rule, it's actually pretty simple.
sentences.zh: 所以参议院的冗长辩论规则其实很简单。

sentences.en: The weird word aside, what it means is that under the Senate rules, it takes 60 votes to advance or cut off debate and get to really consider the meat of a bill, which means that
sentences.zh: 抛开这个奇怪的词不谈，它的意思是根据参议院规则，需要60票才能推进或切断辩论，并真正开始审议法案的核心内容，这意味着

sentences.en: effectively, unless, you know, proponents of a bill control 60 votes, they can never get to a vote on its final passage.
sentences.zh: 实际上，除非法案的支持者掌握了60票，否则他们永远无法进入最终通过的投票环节。

sentences.en: And it's been used in recent years by both parties to block the consideration of bills that they don't support.
sentences.zh: 近年来，两党都曾利用这一点来阻止审议他们不支持的法案。

sentences.en: So in this case, with the voting rights bill today, Republicans didn't have to stand up there and give speeches all day.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情况下，对于今天的投票权法案，共和党人不必站在那里整天发表演讲。

sentences.en: They didn't have to prove any endurance tests.
sentences.zh: 他们不必接受任何耐力测试。

sentences.en: All they had to do was deny this bill, that's 60 votes, to move forward.
sentences.zh: 他们所要做的就是不给这项法案推进所需的60票。

sentences.en: And with the Senate split 50-50 and Republicans all opposed to this, that was not that hard to do.
sentences.zh: 而且由于参议院两党势均力敌（50对50）且共和党人全体反对，这并不是很难做到。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They did it by a wide margin.
sentences.zh: 他们以压倒性优势做到了这一点。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: It was quickly slapped down by Republicans who have more than enough votes.
sentences.zh: 它很快被拥有充足票数的共和党人否决了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, Nick, now that this bill, which has been described by many people as Democrats' most ambitious plan to protect voting rights, now that that has gone down in flames, I want to
sentences.zh: 那么，尼克，既然这项被许多人描述为民主党保护投票权最具雄心的计划已经彻底泡汤了，我想

sentences.en: talk about why the bill failed and the larger meaning and the lessons of its failure.
sentences.zh: 谈谈这项法案失败的原因，以及它失败的更深层意义和教训。

sentences.en: So what would you say that those are?
sentences.zh: 那么你会说这些是什么呢？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Three things come to mind, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想到了三件事。

sentences.en: And the first one just has to do with how big and sprawling and, you know, frankly, imperfect this bill turned out to be for this present moment.
sentences.zh: 第一件事与这项法案在目前显得多么庞大、杂乱而且坦率地说不够完美有关。

sentences.en: What exactly do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你具体是什么意思？

sentences.en: So this was written after the 2018 midterm elections when Democrats, if you remember at
sentences.zh: 所以这是在2018年中期选举之后起草的，当时民主党人如果你们还记得的话

sentences.en: the time, ran and won back control of the House on kind of an anti-corruption, good government,
sentences.zh: 通过打着反腐败、良政、

sentences.en: we're going to put a check on Donald Trump and what we see as his corrupt presidency.
sentences.zh: 我们要对唐纳德·特朗普及其在我们看来腐败的总统任期进行制衡的旗号，参加竞选并赢回了众议院的控制权。

sentences.en: And this bill is just huge, Michael.
sentences.zh: 而这个法案太庞大了，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I mean, it's like 800 pages and touches almost everything you could think of in the electoral process.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它有大约800页，几乎触及了你能在选举过程中想到的所有事情。

sentences.en: You know, it eliminates state voter ID laws.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它取消了各州的选民身份证法。

sentences.en: It creates automatic voter registration across the country.
sentences.zh: 它在全国范围内创建了自动选民登记制度。

sentences.en: It would give the right back to millions of former felons to cast their votes.
sentences.zh: 它将把投票权还给数百万有前科的前罪犯。

sentences.en: It would require super PACs to disclose their donors.
sentences.zh: 它将要求超级政治行动委员会披露其捐赠者。

sentences.en: It would require the president to release his tax returns.
sentences.zh: 它将要求总统公布其纳税申报表。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: You know, the list goes on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，名单还在继续。

sentences.en: It would eliminate partisan gerrymandering in congressional districts.
sentences.zh: 它将取消国会选区中的党派划界操纵。

sentences.en: So this is a really expansive bill.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常广泛的法案。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that size is because, frankly, you know, this bill was written at a time when it was essentially meant to be a messaging bill, a wish list of democratic priorities that was
sentences.zh: 它的规模之所以这么大，是因为坦率地说，你知道，这个法案起草时基本上只是一份宣示立场的法案，是一份民主党优先事项的愿望清单，当时并

sentences.en: not ready to become law.
sentences.zh: 没有准备好成为法律。

sentences.en: So there are often a couple types of bills on Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 所以国会山通常有几种类型的法案。

sentences.en: There's what we call messaging bills, as I just referred to this.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才提到的，有我们所谓的宣示性法案。

sentences.en: And then there are substantive bills that might become law.
sentences.zh: 然后是有可能成为法律的实质性法案。

sentences.en: And messaging bills are usually written to make political points.
sentences.zh: 宣示性法案通常是为了表达政治观点而起草的。

sentences.en: And so they may actually be hard to implement or parts of them might be contradictory.
sentences.zh: 因此它们实际上可能很难实施，或者其中的某些部分可能是矛盾的。

sentences.en: Or, you know, maybe a senator says, I'm willing to support that in theory because they know it'll never become law.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，也许某个参议员会说，我在理论上愿意支持这一点，因为他们知道它永远不会成为法律。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It sounds like you're saying this bill was never really designed to go from being a piece of symbolism to a piece of law.
sentences.zh: 听起来你的意思是，这个法案从一开始就不是为了从象征性文件变成法律文件而设计的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It was not another way of putting it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说并非如此。

sentences.en: It wasn't exactly ready for prime time.
sentences.zh: 它并没有完全准备好登上大舞台。

sentences.en: But fast forward to January of this year, Democrats had won back the White House.
sentences.zh: 但快进到今年1月，民主党人赢回了白宫。

sentences.en: They knew they had held on narrowly to the House.
sentences.zh: 他们知道自己勉强保住了众议院。

sentences.en: And on January 5th, they win two runoff elections in Georgia and claim the sparest of Senate majorities.
sentences.zh: 而在1月5日，他们在佐治亚州赢得了两场决选，并获得了极其微弱的参议院多数席位。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, for the first time in a decade, they've got control of all of Washington.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，十年来第一次，他们掌控了整个华盛顿。

sentences.en: And so, you know, what was a hypothetical becomes a real possibility.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，曾经的假设变成了一种现实的可能性。

sentences.en: Now, at that point, many of the advocacy groups who have made this bill one of their top priorities decided this is actually our opportunity now.
sentences.zh: 当时，许多将该法案列为首要任务的倡导团体决定，这实际上是我们的机会。

sentences.en: And at the same time, Republicans in state houses across the country start under the auspices
sentences.zh: 与此同时，全国各地的州议会中的共和党人开始以特朗普的选举谎言为名义

sentences.en: of Trump's election lies, moving forward with restrictive voting laws that make it harder,
sentences.zh: 推进限制性投票法，专家称这使得有色人种和年轻人更难投票，在某些情况下将权力转移给党派色彩浓厚的立法机构，而不是无党派的选举机构。

sentences.en: experts say, for people of color, for young people to vote, that shift power to partisan legislatures in some cases, rather than nonpartisan election authorities.
sentences.zh: 专家称这使得有色人种和年轻人更难投票，在某些情况下将权力转移给党派色彩浓厚的立法机构，而不是无党派的选举机构。

sentences.en: And Democrats start to feel an urgency to move on this.
sentences.zh: 民主党人开始感受到采取行动的紧迫性。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they reach back into their legislative satchel where they have this massive but quite imperfect messaging bill on voting.
sentences.zh: 于是他们重新翻找立法行囊，里面装着这份庞大但很不完善的投票权宣示性法案。

sentences.en: And it sounds like they decide to put that forward.
sentences.zh: 听起来他们决定把这个推向前台。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没多久。

sentences.en: And so the House quickly passes it in the spring.
sentences.zh: 所以在春季，众议院迅速通过了它。

sentences.en: And then it kicks over to the Senate, where Democrats always knew they were going to have
sentences.zh: 然后它被踢到了参议院，民主党人一直都知道他们将在那里

sentences.en: a fight on their hands because Republicans had no trouble opposing this thing at the outset.
sentences.zh: 面临一场硬仗，因为共和党人从一开始就毫无困难地反对这东西。

sentences.en: But as it happened, it wasn't just Republicans that all of a sudden were looking at this bill and thinking, I'm not so sure about this.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，不仅仅是共和党人突然看着这个法案并心想：我对这个不太确定。

sentences.en: Again, when you take a messaging bill and try and make it a real one, concerns emerged.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，当你把一份宣示性法案试图变成真正法案时，担忧就浮现了。

sentences.en: So the most notable senatorial objector who we're all familiar with, Joe Manchin of West
sentences.zh: 因此，我们都熟悉的、最著名的参议院反对者——来自西弗吉尼亚州的乔·曼钦

sentences.en: Virginia, had actually been a co-sponsor of this bill in the last Congress.
sentences.zh: 实际上在上届国会中曾是该法案的共同提案人。

sentences.en: But this time, when it was reintroduced, he held his name off of it.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，当它被重新提出时，他没有将自己的名字署在上面。

sentences.en: And Manchin said, hey, I've got some issues with this bill.
sentences.zh: 曼钦说，嘿，我对这个法案有一些问题。

sentences.en: And what were those issues, given he had previously co-sponsored it?
sentences.zh: 考虑到他以前曾是共同提案人，那些问题是什么？

sentences.en: So on the one hand, he said, well, first of all, we're just in a different moment here.
sentences.zh: 一方面，他说，首先，我们现在处在一个不同的时期。

sentences.en: There's all kinds of doubt about our elections.
sentences.zh: 对我们的选举存在各种各样的怀疑。

sentences.en: And I think that one of the worst things we could do right now is move forward with a bill on a partisan basis that's just, it's going to end up backfiring on us and making
sentences.zh: 我认为我们现在能做的最糟糕的事情之一，就是以党派基础推进一项法案，最终这会适得其反，使

sentences.en: trust in elections less.
sentences.zh: 人们对选举的信任度下降。

sentences.en: But then he also says, you know, this bill is just too sweeping.
sentences.zh: 但接着他也说，你知道，这个法案太激进了。

sentences.en: He didn't like specific provisions that would have essentially neutered all voter ID laws in states across the country.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢那些基本上会废除全国各州所有选民身份证法的具体条款。

sentences.en: Manchin likes voter ID laws, as it happens to a lot of voters, including Democrats.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，曼钦喜欢选民身份证法，就像许多选民（包括民主党人）一样。

sentences.en: He didn't like a provision that would have set up a campaign financing system for congressional candidates.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢一项为国会候选人建立竞选筹资系统的条款。

sentences.en: Nick, the inevitable question would seem to be, why didn't Democrats just rewrite this old election bill that was first introduced as a messaging bill in 2018 and make it more of
sentences.zh: 尼克，不可避免的问题似乎是，为什么民主党人不干脆重写这个最初在2018年作为宣示性法案提出的老选举法案，让它更接近

sentences.en: a real world bill that could actually pass in the Senate?
sentences.zh: 能够在参议院真正通过的现实法案呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great question, especially looking back from this vantage point.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是个很好的问题，尤其是从现在的角度回看。

sentences.en: But I think there were some different factors going on.
sentences.zh: 但我认为当时有一些不同的因素在起作用。

sentences.en: So one is that this bill really mashed up a lot of different interests that are represented
sentences.zh: 其中一个原因是，这个法案确实将左翼强大倡导团体代表的许多不同利益交织在了一起

sentences.en: by powerful advocacy groups on the left, groups that are interested in dark money, groups that are interested in voting and redistricting of congressional districts.
sentences.zh: 对黑钱感兴趣的团体，对投票和国会选区重新划分感兴趣的团体。

sentences.en: All these different groups had an interest in this bill and locked arms and said, you know, we need all of our pieces to stay in, to stay in it.
sentences.zh: 所有这些不同的利益集团都对这个法案感兴趣，并携手表示，你知道，我们需要保留所有的条款，留在里面。

sentences.en: We need all of our issues to continue to be represented here.
sentences.zh: 我们需要我们的所有议题继续在这里得到代表。

sentences.en: And they also know in the context of this pitch battle that, you know, Republicans are not going to be more favorable to a narrower, more tailored voting bill.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也知道，在这场激烈的争斗背景下，你知道，共和党人不会对一个更狭隘、更有针对性的投票法案更友好。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just not going to win more votes in the United States Senate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它在美国参议院根本赢不了更多选票。

sentences.en: So, you know, if we're going to go forward, let's go forward big with what we believe in, we can try and address some of the technical flaws and amendments along the way.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果我们打算前进，那就带着我们的信仰轰轰烈烈地前进，我们可以在前进的道路上通过修正案来解决一些技术缺陷。

sentences.en: But we're going to try to get this whole thing across the finish line.
sentences.zh: 但我们要努力让整个法案冲过终点线。

sentences.en: The other thing going on is that, you know, they know that looming at the end of this may be a battle over the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 另一件正在发生的事情是，你知道，他们知道在这场斗争的尽头可能潜藏着一场关于冗长辩论的战斗。

sentences.en: And I think the theory is that the bigger, the bolder, the more impactful this bill is for the left, the more force it gives as it crashes into the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为其理论在于，这项法案对左翼而言规模越大、越大胆、冲击力越强，它在撞击冗长辩论阻挠时产生的力量就越大。

sentences.en: And maybe, just maybe, that will be enough to create some cracks and lead Senate Democrats who have been uncomfortable with this so far to change the rules.
sentences.zh: 也许，哪怕只有一点点可能，这也足以制造一些裂痕，并引导那些迄今为止对此感到不安的参议院民主党人去改变规则。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，去看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你尚未订阅《纽约时报》，请在今天下载《时报》应用，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Nick, of course, as we now know, Democrats did not come together to try to change the rules of the Senate to kill the filibuster in order to try to pass this voting rights bill.
sentences.zh: 尼克，当然，正如我们现在所知道的那样，民主党人并没有团结起来试图改变参议院规则以废除冗长辩论阻挠，从而试图通过这项投票权法案。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I think that brings me to my second takeaway from today, which is that Democrats, at this point at least, don't really seem to have much of a chance of getting rid of the
sentences.zh: 所以我想这让我想到了今天总结出的第二点，那就是民主党人，至少在目前这个节点上，似乎真的没什么机会摆脱

sentences.en: filibuster rule.
sentences.zh: 冗长辩论阻挠规则。

sentences.en: They had argued, you know, really going back months now, that this legislation, given its
sentences.zh: 他们一直辩称，你知道，真的可以追溯到几个月前，鉴于这项立法具有

sentences.en: moral weight, it's dealing with the foundations of democracy and the vote itself, was the best argument that they could make.
sentences.zh: 道德分量，它处理的是民主的基础以及选票本身，这是他们能够提出的最佳论点。

sentences.en: It's the tip of the spear colliding into the filibuster that would create a rationale to convince all 50 Senate Democrats and the vice president to change the Senate rules, to
sentences.zh: 它是撞击冗长辩论阻挠的矛尖，这将创造一种理由来说服全部50名参议院民主党人和副总统去改变参议院规则，将

sentences.en: bring that vote down, the threshold down from 60 votes to 50 votes, so that a simple majority can start debate and vote to pass a bill.
sentences.zh: 投票门槛从60票降至50票，以便简单多数可以开始辩论并通过一项法案。

sentences.en: And Democrats, in essence, could go around Republicans to enact not just this big voting bill, but other planks of their agenda as well.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，民主党人可以绕过共和党人，不仅颁布这项重大的投票法案，还能颁布其议程的其他核心内容。

sentences.en: But instead, what we saw on Tuesday, as this vote was filibustered on the floor of the Senate,
sentences.zh: 但相反，我们在周二看到的情况是，当这项投票在参议院大厅遭到冗长辩论阻挠时，

sentences.en: is that Democrats could not organize themselves, at least not all of them, around this idea of getting rid of the filibuster and did not seem to actually be any closer to doing so.
sentences.zh: 是民主党人无法围绕摆脱冗长辩论阻挠这一想法将自己组织起来，至少并非所有人都能如此，而且似乎距离真正做到这一点并没有更近一步。

sentences.en: So if Democrats can't lock arms and get rid of the filibuster over this issue, then the thinking goes, and the Nick Fandos takeaway would be that Democrats are now going to be
sentences.zh: 因此，如果民主党人无法在这个问题上紧密团结并废除冗长辩论阻挠，那么主流观点以及尼克·范多斯的总结就会认为，民主党人现在将被

sentences.en: locked into a dynamic where Republicans can and probably will filibuster almost every major piece of the Biden legislative agenda.
sentences.zh: 锁定在这样一种动态中：共和党人能够而且可能会对拜登立法议程的几乎每一项重大议案进行冗长辩论阻挠。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And the result is that, you know, but for a few types of issues that can move through the
sentences.zh: 其结果是，你知道的，除了少数可以通过

sentences.en: arcane budget reconciliation process, Democrats are going to be looking at a pretty unified
sentences.zh: 神秘的预算调解程序推进的问题之外，民主党人在这一系列对

sentences.en: Republican bloc of opposition on this whole range of issues that, you know, is central to their political platform and to President Biden's administration.
sentences.zh: 他们的政治纲领和拜登总统政府至关重要的问题上，将面对一个相当团结的共和党反对派阵营。

sentences.en: And so, Nick, how do the Democratic senators who refuse to offer up the decisive votes to
sentences.zh: 所以，尼克，那些拒绝在像投票权法案、选举法案这样

sentences.en: end the filibuster on an issue like this voting rights bill, this election bill, how do they
sentences.zh: 的问题上提供决定性票数以结束冗长辩论阻挠的民主党参议员，他们是如何

sentences.en: explain their decision to, in many people's eyes, kind of seal their party's fate for the
sentences.zh: 向公众解释他们的决定的？在许多人眼中，这似乎为他们的党派在

sentences.en: next three year and kind of sentence themselves to a world in which they will get filibustered
sentences.zh: 未来三年的命运盖棺定论了，并判处自己进入这样一个世界：他们将在一遍又一遍的冗长辩论阻挠中

sentences.en: and blocked over and over and over again, even on issues that their party considers to have the highest moral calling?
sentences.zh: 不断受阻，甚至在那些被其党派认为具有最高道德感召力的问题上也是如此？

sentences.en: So I think that we should look at the two most outspoken defenders of the filibuster here in the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们应该看看民主党内对冗长辩论阻挠最直言不讳的两个捍卫者。

sentences.en: So that's Joe Manchin from West Virginia, who we were talking about earlier, and Kyrsten Sinema
sentences.zh: 也就是我们刚才谈到的来自西弗吉尼亚州的乔·曼钦，以及亚利桑那州的

sentences.en: of Arizona, both of them argue essentially that the filibuster is an important tool for promoting civility, bipartisanship, and lasting policy in the Senate, that it tempers the
sentences.zh: 克尔斯滕·西内马，他们两人基本上都认为，冗长辩论阻挠是促进参议院的文明、两党合作以及持久政策的重要工具，它能够缓和

sentences.en: partisan vigor of both parties and leads to better policy down the line.
sentences.zh: 两党的党派狂热，并从长远来看带来更好的政策。

sentences.en: And so they would argue, yeah, voting rights is hugely important to us.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会辩称，是的，投票权对我们极其重要。

sentences.en: Sinema has been a vocal proponent of this legislation.
sentences.zh: 西内马一直是这项立法的大声倡导者。

sentences.en: But, you know, if we pass this now, if we change the rules and we pass this now without
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果我们现在通过这个，如果我们改变规则，并且在没有

sentences.en: Republican support, what's to stop them in the future from getting retribution, from not only reversing all of these things, but putting in place draconian national voting
sentences.zh: 共和党支持的情况下通过了这个，当他们在未来夺回权力时，有什么能阻止他们进行报复，不仅推翻所有这些东西，还要制定严厉的全国投票

sentences.en: laws when they win back power?
sentences.zh: 法律呢？

sentences.en: It's not good for long-term policymaking and continuity of government to be flip-flopping like that.
sentences.zh: 像那样反复摇摆对长期制定政策和政府的连续性是没有好处的。

sentences.en: And we'll rue the day that we got rid of the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 我们将会为废除冗长辩论阻挠的那一天感到后悔。

sentences.en: But in any case, they have laid down a pretty clear line months ago, and they've been unwilling
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，他们在几个月前就划出了一条相当清晰的红线，并且一直不愿

sentences.en: to cross it, despite, you know, millions of dollars being spent in TV ads, rallies being
sentences.zh: 跨过去，尽管你知道，数百万美元被花在电视广告上，集会在

sentences.en: held in their states, you know, the full force of the left pushing on their backs to try and get over that line.
sentences.zh: 他们的州举行，你知道，左翼的全部力量都在他们背后推着，试图让他们越过那条红线。

sentences.en: So for senators like Manchin and Sinema, their view is that when it comes to the moral high ground, that is in not changing the rules of the Senate to end the filibuster, rather
sentences.zh: 因此，对于像曼钦和西内马这样的参议员来说，他们的观点是，当谈到占据道德制高点时，那是在于不改变参议院规则来结束冗长辩论阻挠，而不是

sentences.en: than changing the rules to pass something that many people in the party say has the greatest moral weight, which is passing an election reform law.
sentences.zh: 改变规则去通过某项被党内许多人认为具有最大道德分量的事情，即通过一项选举改革法。法案。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They seem to think that the principle of the filibuster is more important in this moment than this particular sweeping elections bill.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎认为，在这个时刻，冗长辩论阻挠的原则比这项特定的全面选举法案更重要。

sentences.en: So Nick, what is your final takeaway from the demise of this election bill?
sentences.zh: 那么尼克，你对这项选举法案的夭折有什么最终的总结吗？

sentences.en: It's a more substantive one to this bill, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，这是一个对该法案更具实质性的总结。

sentences.en: And it's that, you know, for months, Democrats had put all their eggs in this big national voting rights fight into this bill and the idea that Congress could roll it back.
sentences.zh: 那就是，几个月来，民主党人把所有的赌注都押在了这场重大的全国投票权之争上，押在了这项法案以及国会能够扭转局面的想法上。

sentences.en: And with them essentially pushed to the sideline for now, or maybe permanently, I think it means
sentences.zh: 随着他们基本上被边缘化，可能是暂时的，也可能是永久的，我认为这意味着

sentences.en: that these states that have already passed laws, there's 14 Republican states that have passed, you know, some versions of restrictive voting laws or changing voting rules.
sentences.zh: 那些已经通过法律的州——有14个共和党执政的州已经通过了某种版本的限制性投票法或修改了投票规则——

sentences.en: Those are going to stand uncontested by Congress.
sentences.zh: 这些法律将不受国会的挑战而继续存在。

sentences.en: And other states that may have similar proposals in the hopper, and there are many of them,
sentences.zh: 而其他可能在酝酿类似提案的州，而且有很多这样的州，

sentences.en: will be able to proceed, you know, without the threat of Congress coming in and overriding them.
sentences.zh: 将能够在没有国会介入并推翻它们的威胁下继续推进。

sentences.en: And so what does that look like on a practical level when it comes to election laws and election restrictions?
sentences.zh: 那么，在涉及选举法和选举限制时，这在实际层面上是什么样的？

sentences.en: It means that across the country in states, and many of them key battleground states, where
sentences.zh: 这意味着在全国各地的各州中，其中许多是关键的摇摆州，

sentences.en: Republican legislatures have passed these new laws, it's going to be harder to, in some cases, request a mail-in ballot.
sentences.zh: 共和党州议会通过了这些新法律，在某些情况下，申请邮寄选票将变得更加困难。

sentences.en: It'll be harder to find a drop box to drop your ballot in.
sentences.zh: 找到投放选票的投递箱将变得更加困难。

sentences.en: It means that it might be harder to vote on Sunday when Black voters often go to the poll.
sentences.zh: 这意味着黑人选民经常去投票的周日投票可能会变得更加困难。

sentences.en: You know, in aggregate, it means that in all these little ways, Republicans in many of these
sentences.zh: 总而言之，这意味着通过所有这些微小的途径，许多关键州的

sentences.en: key states are putting in place a set of rules that, especially in a close election, could
sentences.zh: 共和党人正在建立一套规则，尤其是在选情胶着的情况下，这些规则可能会

sentences.en: tip the balance in their favor and benefit Republican candidates, make it easier for their voters
sentences.zh: 使天平向他们倾斜，并使共和党候选人受益，让他们选民的投票变得更容易，

sentences.en: to get to the polls, and harder for the type of people who vote for Democrats to cast their ballot or to win election challenges in contested cases.
sentences.zh: 而让那些投票给民主党的人投票或在有争议的选举诉讼中赢得胜利变得更加困难。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And with congressional legislation now foreclosed, it would seem the only option left would be the courts.
sentences.zh: 随着国会立法现在被堵死，唯一的选择似乎只剩下法院了。

sentences.en: And our colleague, Adam Liptak, told us earlier this week that it looks to him that the Supreme
sentences.zh: 我们的同事亚当·利普塔克在本周早些时候告诉我们，在他看来，最高

sentences.en: Court is likely to uphold these Republican-led restrictions that you just described.
sentences.zh: 法院可能会维持你刚才描述的这些由共和党主导的限制措施。

sentences.en: And so, taken together, it would look like neither of those branches of government are going to step in and challenge these state restrictions.
sentences.zh: 因此，综上所述，看起来政府的这两个分支都不会介入并挑战这些州的限制措施。

sentences.en: I think that's true on a big scale at the moment.
sentences.zh: 我认为从目前的大局来看确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, Democrats in Congress are sure as heck going to keep trying on this issue, but for all the reasons we laid out, it's hard to see how they'll have success anytime soon,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，国会中的民主党人肯定会继续在这个问题上努力，但由于我们列出的所有原因，很难看到他们能在短期内取得成功，

sentences.en: certainly before the 2022 election.
sentences.zh: 当然在2022年选举之前是很难的。

sentences.en: And in the courts, you know, there's all kinds of institutional groups and state legislators that will continue to sue to try and block these.
sentences.zh: 而在法院方面，你知道，有各种各样的体制内团体和州议员将继续起诉，试图阻止这些措施。

sentences.en: And they may win some piecemeal victories, but it's kind of a losing game of whack-a-mole, I think, for those who are trying to stand in the way of these things.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会取得一些零星的胜利，但我认为，对于那些试图阻挠这些事情的人来说，这就像是一场打地鼠的必输游戏。

sentences.en: Maybe they'll be successful here or there.
sentences.zh: 也许他们在某个地方会成功。

sentences.en: But overall, there seems to be a green light for Republicans, you know, in favor of these kind of restrictions to just keep stacking them up.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，对于倾向于这种限制的共和党人来说，似乎亮起了绿灯，让他们可以继续叠加这些措施。

sentences.en: And practically speaking, that really only leaves Democrats with a couple of options.
sentences.zh: 从实际角度来看，这实际上只给民主党人留下了几个选择。

sentences.en: One is really just to try and make this a political issue, to put democracy on the ballot
sentences.zh: 一个是真正试图将这变成一个政治议题，在接下来的选举中把

sentences.en: in the next elections and say, Republicans are not only standing in the way of all these popular
sentences.zh: 民主推上选票，并表示：共和党人不仅阻挠了我们认为你们作为选民希望政府去做的所有这些受欢迎的

sentences.en: policy positions that we think you as voters want to see your government do, but they're stopping us from even protecting your right to vote.
sentences.zh: 政策立场，而且他们还在阻止我们保护你们的投票权。

sentences.en: And they don't deserve a seat at the table.
sentences.zh: 他们不配在决策桌上占有一席之地。

sentences.en: You've got to vote them out.
sentences.zh: 你们必须用选票把他们赶下台。

sentences.en: You've got to bring us back in bigger numbers so we can get this done because your very ability to vote and have your government be responsive to you is on the line.
sentences.zh: 你们必须以更大的规模把我们选回来，这样我们才能完成这项工作，因为你们投票的能力以及政府对你们做出回应的能力正处于危急关头。

sentences.en: So perhaps that explains why Democrats even held this vote in the Senate on Tuesday, knowing
sentences.zh: 所以这或许可以解释为什么民主党人甚至在周二于参议院举行了这次投票，明知

sentences.en: full well that they would lose, knowing full well that this was not going to be the impetus
sentences.zh: 自己会输，明知这不会成为

sentences.en: to get rid of the filibuster because they wanted to put it on record that Republicans opposed this bill so they could use it as an issue in the next set of elections.
sentences.zh: 摆脱冗长辩论阻挠的契机，因为他们希望留下记录，证明共和党人反对这项法案，这样他们就可以将其作为下一轮选举中的一个议题来使用。

sentences.en: Yes, failing, you know, this creating the kind of pressure they need to get rid of the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 是的，既然未能创造出他们摆脱冗长辩论阻挠所需的压力，

sentences.en: Democrats are very much looking down the pike here at the next election and are trying to, you know, portray the Republican Party as an anti-democratic force, you know, still in
sentences.zh: 民主党人正将目光投向接下来的选举，并试图将共和党人描绘成一股反民主的力量，他们仍然

sentences.en: league with Donald Trump and out to undermine the system of government and portray themselves as Democrats as protectors of that.
sentences.zh: 与唐纳德·特朗普沆瀣一气，企图破坏政府体制，而将自己描绘成民主的捍卫者。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But the dilemma would seem to be that between now and the next election, Democrats may get locked
sentences.zh: 但两难的境地似乎在于，从现在到下次选举之间，民主党人可能会被锁定在

sentences.en: into this dynamic we just described, which is that they really can't get much passed because of the filibuster, which wasn't changed because of this bill.
sentences.zh: 我们刚才描述的这种动态中，即由于冗长辩论阻挠（该法案未能改变这一点），他们实际上无法通过太多法案。

sentences.en: And therefore, they need to wave their failures around to voters and say, we were never given a chance because Republicans wouldn't give it to us.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们需要向选民到处宣扬他们的失败，并说：我们从来没有得到过机会，因为共和党人不给我们机会。

sentences.en: And will voters side with them or will voters say, you didn't get anything done, we should give Republicans a chance?
sentences.zh: 选民会站在他们一边，还是会说：你们什么也没干成，我们应该给共和党一个机会？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that that's a question that's causing a lot of anxiety for Democrats right now.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个目前给民主党人带来极大焦虑的问题。

sentences.en: You know, they were quick out of the gate to pass this whopping $2 trillion stimulus bill and they did it fast and it was very popular.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们迅速推出了高达2万亿美元的刺激法案，而且动作很快，非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's starting to look very quickly like they may not have much luck getting much of their agenda through the Congress.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，情况很快看起来他们可能没有什么好运气能让自己的大部分议程通过国会。

sentences.en: They may be able to get a big infrastructure and jobs bill through.
sentences.zh: 他们或许能通过一项大规模的基础设施和就业法案。

sentences.en: But after that, progressives say, our voters are going to look at us in 2022.
sentences.zh: 但在此之后，进步派表示，我们的选民将在2022年看着我们，

sentences.en: And say, hey, we gave you all three levers of government.
sentences.zh: 并说：嘿，我们把政府的所有三个权力杠杆都交给了你们，

sentences.en: We turned out in huge numbers last time and this is all we got for it.
sentences.zh: 我们上次以极高的投票率支持了你们，而这就是我们得到的全部结果。

sentences.en: I think with a hand of cards that they've been dealt, Democratic leaders feel like we've got to at least try to play this political card and hang it on Republicans.
sentences.zh: 我认为，凭借他们被发到的这副牌，民主党领袖们觉得我们至少得试着打出这张政治牌，并将责任归咎于共和党。

sentences.en: But the question is, how powerful and effective politically can Democrats claiming the moral
sentences.zh: 但问题是，在那些支持这些限制措施的共和党人正在亲自书写选举规则的竞赛中，民主党人声称自己占据

sentences.en: high ground as the protector of democracy really be in a contest where Republicans who have backed these restrictions are writing the rules of the election itself?
sentences.zh: 作为民主保护者的道德制高点，究竟能有多大的政治权势和效力？

sentences.en: Thank you, Nick.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，尼克。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，迈克尔。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, the Republican governor of Texas, Greg Abbott, moved his state closer to adopting sweeping restrictions on voting.
sentences.zh: 周二，德克萨斯州共和党州长格雷格·阿博特推动该州更接近于通过全面的投票限制措施。

sentences.en: Abbott called a special session of the state's legislature, during which Republicans are expected
sentences.zh: 阿博特召集了该州立法机构的特别会议，预计共和党人将在会议期间

sentences.en: to pass a bill that would make it harder to vote by mail, ban both drive-thru and 24-hour voting, and give much greater power to partisan poll watchers.
sentences.zh: 通过一项法案，该法案将使邮寄投票变得更加困难，禁止免下车投票和24小时投票，并赋予党派监票员更大的权力。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: So how are we doing?
sentences.zh: 那么我们做得怎么样？

sentences.en: Today, I want to drill down on the numbers that show where we have made the most progress and where we have more work to do.
sentences.zh: 今天，我想深入研究那些显示我们在哪里取得了最大进展以及在哪里还有更多工作要做的数字。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, the Biden administration said that it would miss its original goal of getting at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine to 70% of adults by July 4th.
sentences.zh: 周二，拜登政府表示，它将无法实现原定于7月4日前让70%的成年人接种至少一剂新冠疫苗的目标。

sentences.en: Where the country has more work to do is particularly with 18 to 26-year-olds.
sentences.zh: 国家还有更多工作要做的地方特别是在18至26岁的人群中。

sentences.en: During a news conference, the president's COVID-19 coordinator, Dr. Jeff Zients, said that it's proven harder than expected to convince younger Americans to take the vaccine.
sentences.zh: 在一次新闻发布会上，总统的新冠疫情协调员杰夫·齐茨博士表示，说服年轻美国人接种疫苗比预期要困难。

sentences.en: The reality is many younger Americans have felt like COVID-19 is not something that impacts them, and they've been less eager to get the shot.
sentences.zh: 现实是，许多年轻的美国人觉得新冠肺炎不是一件会影响到他们的事情，他们接种疫苗的积极性较低。

sentences.en: Older Americans continue to take the vaccine at high rates.
sentences.zh: 年长的美国人继续以高比率接种疫苗。

sentences.en: 87% of those 65 or older have gotten at least one dose.
sentences.zh: 65岁及以上的人中有87%已经接种了至少一剂。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由安妮·布朗、妮娜·鲍特克和斯特拉·陈制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn and engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩编辑，克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barrow.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了许多自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《都市》的最新一期节目中，我和萨拉·科尼格一起，为您讲述那些试图维持自身影响力却在过程中失去控制的人们的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何地方收听。
